pages.text: After autumn rain, mushrooms popped up in the forest. Grandpa took a basket.
Mushroom soup tonight. Nils wanted to pick the mushrooms himself. "I know mushrooms! They're round."
"Show me before picking," said Grandpa. Barely answering, Nils scurried toward the bushes.
He pulled out mushrooms. Big, small, colorful.
Soon his basket was piled high. "I picked the most!"
Grandpa set the basket on his knees and checked them one by one. This here, that there. Two piles.
"These are edible. These aren't. Eating them hurts your tummy." The inedible pile was a mountain. Only three were edible.
Grandpa placed an edible mushroom in Nils's hand. "Ask about what you don't know. There's no shame in it."
Nils held up a mushroom. "This one?" Grandpa nodded. "Yes, edible!"
That evening, mushroom soup bubbled. Nils's mushrooms floated in the pot. "I asked before picking these!"
